newsitem.title: UK: Crude oil tanker rates fall for W. Africa/Europe.
newsitem.headline: Crude oil tanker rates fall for W. Africa/Europe.

text.p: Crude oil tanker chartering rates were steady to weaker in a number of sectors on Thursday with 130,000 tonne Suezmax rates from West Africa to Europe taking the biggest fall, shipbrokers said.
"Suezmax rates (for West Africa-Europe journeys) have now lost 10 points or so in just a couple of days," one broker said. "There is not much going on."

Repsol's fixture of the 130,000 tonne Choctaw from West Africa to Spain at W80 was seen representative, while rates for similar sized vessels sailing from West Africa to the U.S. Atlantic Coast were assessed steady to weaker at around W85.
"Owners are scared of Christmas and don't want to be left with tankers they can't fix," one broker said.

Cross-Med rates for Suezmaxes were steady, despite news that Shell had fixed the 135,000 tonne Svenner at a low W80. Brokers said the Svenner was fixed below market because it was an old ship, and they assessed rates closer to W92.5. Dealers said weather was improving, which may further depress rates. Aframaxes were worth W105-W107.5 for cross-Med voyages.
Inter-UK/Cont rates were steady with at least two fixtures noted at around W97.5-W100 for 80,000 tonne Aframaxes.
"I can't see these numbers changing much," one dealer said.
Mideast-Japan rates for 250,000 tonne very large crude carriers (VLCCs) were steady, and four early January cargoes were chartered at between W61.25 and W63.5.
Caribs markets were little changed for 70,000 tonners and brokers saw vessels worth around W150 for Caribs/USG voyages.
Lessening activity in Mediterranean fuel oil markets was pressuring rates lower and 25,000 tonne tankers were thought to be worth around W195.
